# Set-up

This markdown contains the code used to apply `CellBender` to all of the engineered datasets (generated [here](Tonsils_10xFlex_make_engineered_datasets.html)). For each of the engineered datasets, an input file for `CellBender` was generated [here](Tonsils_10xFlex_make_engineered_CellbenderInput.html)

## Load libraries

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(readr)
  library(here)
  library(Seurat)
  library(scater)
  library(qs2)
  library(DropletUtils)
})

```



# Running `CellBender` using GPU

`CellBender` is run through an sbatch script which can be found here: `code/Tonsil_10xFlex/Engineered/run_CellBender_EngineeredDatasets.sbatch`. This code was run using our HPC system to access GPU. 

To make the code accessible via workflowR website, we've pasted the content of the sbatch script in the code chunk below:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --partition=rhel_gpu
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:T4:1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --mem=48G
#SBATCH --time=00-04:00:00

set -euo pipefail

# INPUT
INPUT_H5="${1}"
SAMPLE="${2}"
SAMPLE_OUT="${SAMPLE}_CellBender"

# Paths
OUTPUT_DIR="$(dirname "${INPUT_H5}")/${SAMPLE_OUT}"

# make output
mkdir -p "${OUTPUT_DIR}"

# Change to output directory
cd "${OUTPUT_DIR}"

# Load required modules
module load cuda/12.4.0-gcc-13.2.0   # for RHEL9
module load miniconda3/24.3.0-gcc-13.2.0   # for RHEL9

# Activate CellBender conda environment
source /config/spack/v0.22.1/opt/spack/linux-rhel9-haswell/gcc-13.2.0/miniconda3-24.3.0-re4lxkwqjaazi6ckedtfhnzrjiefmhei/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate cellbender_v3.0.2

# Run CellBender remove‑background
cellbender remove-background \
    --input  "${INPUT_H5}" \
    --output "${OUTPUT_DIR}/${SAMPLE_OUT}.h5" \
    --expected-cells 12000 \
    --total-droplets-included 45000 \
    --cuda \
    --learning-rate 0.000001

# Make compatible with seurat
ptrepack --complevel 5 ${SAMPLE_OUT}.h5:/matrix ${SAMPLE_OUT}_seurat.h5:/matrix

echo "✅ CellBender completed for ${SAMPLE}. Outputs in ${OUTPUT_DIR}"

```


For each of the generated `h5` input files, a run script was submitted:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#!/bin/bash

INPUT_DIR="/oshlack_lab/michelle.meier/projects/ambient_doublet_singlecell/output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Engineered/"

for INPUT_H5 in "${INPUT_DIR}"/Tonsils_10xFlex_engineered_12k_0.15p_*s_cellbenderInput_feature_bc_matrix.h5
do
    SAMPLE=$(basename "${INPUT_H5}" \
        "_cellbenderInput_feature_bc_matrix.h5")

    sbatch \
        --job-name="run_cellbender_${SAMPLE}" \
        --output="/oshlack_lab/michelle.meier/projects/ambient_doublet_singlecell/code/Tonsil_10xFlex/Engineered/cellbender_logs/run_CellBender_${SAMPLE}_%j.out" \
        --error="/oshlack_lab/michelle.meier/projects/ambient_doublet_singlecell/code/Tonsil_10xFlex/Engineered/cellbender_logs/run_CellBender_${SAMPLE}_%j.err" \
        run_CellBender_EngineeredDatasets.sbatch "${INPUT_H5}" "${SAMPLE}"

done
```

The error and log files for each job can be found in this folder: `code/Tonsil_10xFlex/Engineered/cellbender_logs`


# Preparing output for further analysis

Next, we will reformat the `CellBender` output to match the 10X output directory structure. In addition, we will only be considering barcodes for the orignal 12k cells are cells, and not use `CellBender`'s cell calling algorithm. 

Set directories for `CellBender` outputs. 

```{r}
cellbender_outs <- list.files(path = here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Engineered/cellbender_output_files"),
                              full.names = T)

#uncorrected objects
uncorrected_paths <- list.files(path = here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Engineered/"),
                              pattern = "Tonsils_10xFlex*.*s$",
                              full.names = T)

```



## Write function

Write a function that reads in `.h5` file, subsets to relevant barcodes and writes output in 10X folder format. We also need to get the uncorrected data to determine how much RNA was removed. 

```{r}
run_makeCellBenderOutput <- function(INDEX){
  #raw metadata
  uncorrected <- read_tsv(paste0(uncorrected_paths[[INDEX]],"/metadata.tsv"), show_col_types = F)
  
  #load cellbender unfiltered counts
  counts <- Read10X_h5(cellbender_outs[[INDEX]])
  counts_f <- counts[, colnames(counts) %in% uncorrected$GEM_barcode]
  
  #add QC metrics to cellbender objects
  sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(counts=counts_f))
  is.mito <- grepl(pattern = "^MT", rownames(sce))
  sce <- addPerCellQCMetrics(sce, subsets = list(mito = is.mito))
  sce$nfeatures_rounded <- colSums(assay(sce, "counts") > 0.5)
  
  rm(counts, counts_f);gc()
  
  #clean
  new_meta <- sce@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>%
    mutate(., GEM_barcode = rownames(.)) %>% 
    dplyr::rename(., ncount =sum ,  nfeatures =detected) %>%
    left_join(.,uncorrected , by="GEM_barcode") %>% 
    mutate(., nfeature_frac_removed = (nfeatures_raw-nfeatures_rounded)/nfeatures_raw,
              ncount_frac_removed = (ncount_raw-ncount)/ncount_raw,
              Barcode = GEM_barcode) %>%
    select(., -c("total", "subsets_mito_detected", "subsets_mito_sum"))
  
  #reorder to match SCE order
  rownames(new_meta) <- new_meta$GEM_barcode
  new_meta <- new_meta[match(colnames(sce), new_meta$GEM_barcode),]
  stopifnot(all(rownames(new_meta) == colnames(sce)))
  
  #export
  out_file <- sprintf("%s/%s_CellBender", 
                      here("output/data/Tonsils_10xFlex/Engineered"),
                      basename(uncorrected_paths[[INDEX]]))
  print("out_file")
  
  DropletUtils::write10xCounts(path = out_file,
                             x = counts(sce),
                             version = "3", 
                             overwrite = TRUE)
  write_tsv(x = new_meta,
          file = sprintf("%s/metadata.tsv", out_file))
}
```


## Run for all engineered datasets


```{r, warning=FALSE, fig.align='center'}

corrected <- sapply(1:length(cellbender_outs), function(IN){
  run_makeCellBenderOutput(INDEX = IN)
})

```
